content.text:
**Result:** Dq ≈ 670 cm⁻¹ (10Dq ≈ 6 700), B ≈ 780 cm⁻¹, C ≈ 3 500 cm⁻¹. Treat these as approximate, because the four bands are not fully self-consistent in the model.

**Method.** I used the tabulated d⁷ high-spin Tanabe–Sugano term energies and fitted by hand-guided trial and error. The three spin-allowed quartet bands fix Dq and B. The spin-forbidden ²T₁(2) band then fixes C.

**Quartet bands.**
- In this model ⁴A₂ − ⁴T₂ = 10Dq exactly. The observed 12 400 − 6 150 = 6 250 cm⁻¹ points to Dq ≈ 625 cm⁻¹.
- The ⁴T₂ position then needs Dq nearer 700 cm⁻¹.
- The ⁴T₁(2) band at 16 850 cm⁻¹ needs B ≈ 750–800 cm⁻¹.
- A three-band fit with the ratio-fit tool gave Dq ≈ 719 cm⁻¹ and B ≈ 788 cm⁻¹.

**Trial calculations.**

| Dq | B | C | ⁴T₂ | ⁴A₂ | ⁴T₁(2) | ²T₁(2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 680 | 740 | 3 000 | 5 913 | 12 713 | 16 125 | 16 740 |
| 650 | 800 | 3 300 | 5 614 | 12 114 | 16 729 | 18 176 |
| observed | | | 6 150 | 12 400 | 16 850 | 19 000 |

**Compromise.** Interpolating between the trials, Dq ≈ 670 cm⁻¹ and B ≈ 780 cm⁻¹ gives ⁴T₂ ≈ 5 800, ⁴A₂ ≈ 12 450 and ⁴T₁(2) ≈ 16 500 cm⁻¹. The ⁴T₂ and ⁴T₁(2) bands come out about 300–400 cm⁻¹ below observed, and ⁴A₂ is within about 100 cm⁻¹.

**C from ²T₁(2).** The ²T₁(2) energy rises by about 3 cm⁻¹ per cm⁻¹ of C. From the trial at Dq = 650, B = 800, C = 3 300 (18 176 cm⁻¹), reaching 19 000 cm⁻¹ needs C ≈ 3 500 cm⁻¹. That gives C/B ≈ 4.5. I did not rerun the final parameter set to check this C value.

**Covalency.** B ≈ 780 cm⁻¹ is about 80% of the free-ion value for Co²⁺ (roughly 970 cm⁻¹), which indicates fairly covalent Co–Cl bonding.
